endorsements.quote: Mitigation strategies such as privacy-preserving training methods (e.g. differential privacy)33 or data augmentation or regularisation to reduce memorisation can reduce these risks,32 but typically involve trade-offs with performance, transparency, and reproducibility.33

Adopting lifecycle practices such as transparent versioning of models, routine regression testing, and documented monitoring helps transform this process into shared, reproducible science, and reduces technical debt to help accelerate progress robustly.36,37

unlisted_practices: Academia should recognise model retraining and maintenance as scholarship rather than mere maintenance.
Journals and funders should incentivise and support the science of how AI model retraining is undertaken.
Developers should release open-source code, model weights, and data-processing pipelines with good documentation to enable reproducibility, benchmarking, and bias testing.
Developers should use layered, domain-specific approaches to openness, such as transparency of methods and assumptions when model weights cannot be shared.
Imaging manufacturers and institutions should adopt standard imaging formats such as DICOM to support interoperability and model retraining.
Researchers and funders should promote the development of diverse public datasets and report population demographics and subgroup performance.
Stakeholders should share best practices and code for model retraining and maintenance, particularly to support resource-limited institutions.
Developers should test model updates for catastrophic forgetting when retraining to ensure continued safe performance.
Researchers should plan to retrain all models over time to remain useful and safe.
